Moment alignment transformer for video-to-video moment retrieval
abstract: Video-to-video moment retrieval (Vid2VidMR) is the task of localizing unseen events or moments in a target video using a query video. This task is challenging due to the need for semantic frame-level alignment and modeling complex dependencies between query and target videos. To address this, we introduce MATR (Moment Alignment TRansformer), a transformer-based model that captures semantic context and temporal detail for precise moment localization. MATR conditions target video representations on query features through dual-stage sequence alignment, encoding the necessary correlations and dependencies. These representations guide foreground/background classification and boundary prediction heads to identify moments in the target video that semantically match the query. To provide strong task-specific initialization, we further propose a self-supervised pre-training objective where the model learns to localize random clips within videos. Extensive experiments show that MATR achieves absolute gains of 15.4% in R@1 and 11.4% in mIoU over state-of-the-art methods on the ActivityNet-VRL dataset, and 16.4% in R@1 and 16.3% in mIoU on our newly proposed SportsMoments dataset. Code is available at: https://github.com/vl2g/MATR.

title: DINOv3 meets sketches: A general sketch-photo encoder
abstract: Sketches are considered a very relevant means of communication for humans. In fact, these abstract images are our first approach to real objects during our early childhood and allow us to unfold complex processes or transmit complex ideas, facilitating understanding. Therefore, it should also be considered an essential element in computer vision. Beyond sketch-based image retrieval, we can leverage sketches to guide other visual tasks, including segmentation or localization. To this end, it is critical to account for a highly effective sketch-based encoder trained in a bimodal fashion with sketches and photos. However, having sketch-photo pairs is unfeasible, so self or weakly supervised learning is required. In addition, given DINOv3's outstanding performance, it is crucial to leverage it to make it applicable to the sketch-based domain while retaining its learned knowledge. Therefore, in this work, we allow DINOv3 to meet sketches by proposing a new sketch-based encoder, \textbf{skDINO}, that demonstrates a general and outstanding effectiveness across different visual tasks. We evaluate our new encoder in zero-shot (ZS-SBIR) and zero-shot fine-grained retrieval (ZS-FG-SBIR). For ZS-SBIR, our proposal improves current models by $24.3\%$, $30.3\%$, and $15.7\%$ in mAP@200 on Flickr15K, eCommerce, and Sketchy datasets, respectively. For ZS-FG-SBIR, our model reaches an improvement of $15.8\%$ in accuracy in the Sketchy dataset. Furthermore, we leverage our encoder for sketch-based segmentation, where our model outperforms the state of the art, achieving a new mIoU of 0.7139, an increase of $18.8\%$ over the best known model.

title: Geometry-aware depth-guided representation learning for structure-preserving low-light image enhancement
abstract: Low-light degradation reduces image visibility and weakens structural cues that are important for visual representation and scene understanding. Existing low-light image enhancement methods mainly focus on appearance restoration, while insufficiently exploiting scene geometry to preserve structural consistency. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a Depth-guided Multi-scale Attention Network (DMSA-Net) for geometry-aware low-light image enhancement. DMSA-Net introduces depth-related structural priors into low-light representation learning through reflectance-geometry interaction. A Retinex-based decomposition module is first used to obtain illumination-invariant reflectance representations, from which depth cues are inferred to characterize scene structure under degraded illumination. A multi-scale depth-guided fusion strategy is then embedded into a hierarchical encoder-decoder architecture, where depth-aware attention adaptively integrates geometric and appearance features. Experiments on several benchmark datasets show that DMSA-Net achieves effective low-light restoration while improving structural preservation. Moreover, we construct LOL-D, a depth-augmented low-light dataset, to facilitate research on geometry-aware low-light vision.

A practical approach to underwater depth and surface normals estimation
abstract: Monocular Depth and Surface Normals Estimation (MDSNE) is crucial for tasks such as three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, autonomous navigation, and underwater exploration. Current methods rely either on discriminative models, which struggle with transparent or reflective surfaces, or generative models, which, while accurate, are computationally expensive. This paper presents a novel deep learning model for Monocular Depth and Surface Normals Estimation (MDSNE), specifically tailored for underwater environments, using a hybrid architecture that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Transformers, leveraging the strengths of both approaches. Training effective MDSNE models is often hampered by noisy real-world datasets and the limited generalization of synthetic datasets. To address this, we generate pseudo-labeled real data using multiple pre-trained MDSNE models. To curate this data without ground-truth supervision, we propose the Depth Normal Evaluation and Selection Algorithm (DNESA), which scores each candidate teacher’s prediction with three intrinsic image-quality cues (multi-scale gradient alignment with the RGB image, image–depth mutual information, and edge-aware total variation) and selects the top-scoring pseudo-label per image. A lightweight student model is then trained on this curated dataset. AquaMDS uses only 7.58 million parameters, 44 × to 113 × smaller than the four state-of-the-art foundation-model teachers it distils from (DepthAnything V2, ZoeDepth, Metric3D V2, and Marigold), and runs at 63 FPS on a single GPU. Despite this efficiency, on USOD10K and Atlantis AquaMDS substantially outperforms every prior similarly-sized baseline method and is competitive with the giant teachers under a unified evaluation protocol; on the small Sea-Thru D3 split AquaMDS sits mid-pack among the giant teachers. Key contributions include: a novel and efficient MDSNE model, the DNESA algorithm, a domain-specific data pipeline, and a focus on real-time performance and scalability. Designed for real-world underwater applications, our model facilitates low-cost deployments in underwater robots and autonomous vehicles, bridging the gap between research and practical implementation.

Trustworthy medical imaging: Conformal prediction with adversarial guarantees
abstract: Adversarial attacks pose significant threats to the reliability and security of deep learning models, particularly in critical domains such as medical imaging. This paper introduces a novel framework designed to address effective prediction under a wide range of models, using various conformal prediction methods, and against adversarial attacks within a predefined threat model space on the test set, including various combinatorial attacks, while ensuring valid coverage. Extensive experiments conducted on the MedMNIST dataset (comprising PathMNIST, OrganAMNIST, and TissueMNIST) demonstrate that our approach can achieve valid coverage under this framework. This work advances the state-of-the-art in uncertainty quantification and adversarial robustness, providing a reliable mechanism for deploying deep learning models in adversarial environments.

title: Efficient semantic segmentation via Lightweight Multiple-Information Interaction Network
BlinkFusionNet: Gated multimodal fusion for robust blink event detection in sign language corpora
abstract: Eye blinks function as important non-manual markers in human communication. In sign languages, their timing often coincides with syntactic boundaries and discourse organisation. Detecting blinks in real-world sign language data remains challenging, as motion blur, rapid facial movement, varying illumination, and frequent hand–face occlusions can obscure eyelid motion and reduce the reliability of unimodal approaches. In this work, we introduce BlinkFusionNet , a deep learning model designed to provide robust blink detection under such conditions. The model integrates three complementary sources of information: visual appearance from RGB frames, short-term motion derived from optical flow, and geometric cues reflecting eye openness based on the eye aspect ratio (EAR) and its temporal variation. A feature-wise gated fusion mechanism adaptively weights these modalities, enabling the model to remain stable when individual cues become unreliable. To capture the temporal dynamics of blink closure and reopening, we incorporate bidirectional temporal modelling. Evaluated on a signer-disjoint split, BlinkFusionNet achieves a window-level Blink F1-score of 0.896 using groups of T = 10 frames. For annotation purposes, we further derive frame-level blink probabilities through sliding-window inference and aggregate them into contiguous blink segments compatible with standard linguistic annotation tools. These properties make BlinkFusionNet a practical and scalable solution.

Multi-cepstral feature integration for audio deepfake detection under domain shift
abstract: Recent advances in speech synthesis and voice conversion technologies have enabled the creation of highly realistic audio deepfakes, posing significant challenges to biometric authentication, digital forensics, and misinformation detection. Although numerous countermeasures have been proposed, many existing approaches rely either on a single acoustic representation or on computationally intensive deep learning architectures, often exhibiting limited robustness when operating conditions differ from those observed during training. This paper investigates a lightweight and interpretable framework for audio deepfake detection based on the integration of multiple complementary cepstral representations. Specifically, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Linear Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (LFCCs), Constant-Q Cepstral Coefficients (CQCCs), and Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCCs) are jointly exploited to capture synthesis-related artifacts across different spectral resolutions and perceptual scales. The resulting feature representation is evaluated using conventional machine learning classifiers under strict speaker-independent protocols. Extensive experiments conducted on the FakeAVCelebV2 and ASVspoof2019 LA benchmarks, together with cross-dataset evaluations on the challenging In-The-Wild Audio (IWA) dataset, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework under both in-domain and out-of-domain conditions. Furthermore, a domain-stability analysis is introduced to investigate the contribution of individual acoustic descriptors to cross-dataset generalization and to identify features that remain robust across different data distributions. The obtained results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating complementary cepstral representations for audio deepfake detection and highlight the importance of feature stability in improving cross-dataset generalization.

Clustering and token denoising for faster and more robust VLMs
abstract: Recent Visual-Language Models (VLMs) have enhanced the capabilities of pre-trained LLMs by adding vision tokens alongside text, with approaches like LLaVA showing impressive results. However, the computational burden of processing up to 576 or 729 visual tokens makes edge deployment challenging. While various token pruning techniques require retraining, some are training-free and thus can easily adapt to architecture changes. We introduce ClustRS, a two-part, training-free algorithm for robust token pruning. Its first component is an attention-weighted, clustering algorithm that selects representative tokens from each semantic cluster. The second component, Residual Shrinkage, is a one-pass denoising step on the selected tokens. These training-free lightweight steps make LLaVA ready for real-world data, improving robustness to a wide range of image-noise types and intensities. Experimental results on the ScienceQA-IMG and MM-VET benchmarks show our method outperforms attention- and diversity-based methods by up to 20% under extreme noise and token conditions (reducing tokens by 97%, down to 16 tokens) on LLaVA 1.5 7b and achieves better results on LLaVA-OneVision, where we match baseline performance with fewer than one-third of their tokens under mild noise conditions. Our study demonstrates a simple yet powerful alternative to both score-only and diversity-only pruning rules, paving the way for compute-efficient and noise-resilient VLM deployment.
